When: Within ninety (90) calendar days from the date of contract award. Where: American Center, U.S. Consulate General Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Why: To modernize the Center's technological capability with high-end American brand /equivalent hardware that projects a premium, high-tech "American look and

ling flawless technical delivery for public diplomacy programming. Goal: Deploy flexible, multi-modal AV and computing infrastructure that supports formal briefings, large public events, and STEM/makerspace programming. Target Audience: Guests of U.S. Consulate General Chennai, VIP/ executive stakeholders, technical teams, and American Center program attendees & visitors. Primary Objective: Deliver fully tested, IT-cleared, American brand / equivalent technology hardware. Statement of Work paragraph 2.1 requires documented evidence of past performance migrating legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365 and the Power Platform. Two questions on this paragraph: a. Is 2.1 a pass or fail responsibility requirement, or is it evaluated as part of the past performance factor described in the evaluation criteria? b. Where an offeror's relevant past performance was performed under commercial contracts rather than federal prime contracts, will the Government accept that commercial past performance? Will the Government also accept the relevant past performance of proposed key personnel or of a proposed subcontractor? Answer: Paragraph 2.1 is evaluated as part of the Government’s technical assessment of the offeror’s relevant past performance and technical competency, rather than as a separate pass/fail responsibility determination. The Government will accept relevant commercial past performance, not just federal prime contract experience, provided the quoted experience demonstrates comparable scope, complexity, and relevance to the requirement. The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions, intends to negotiate and award a ﬁrm-ﬁxed-price purchase order on a non-competitive basis to Xact Metal, Inc., 200 Innovation Blvd, Ste 257, State College, PA 16803 for one (1) Advanced Metal Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) 3D Printing System, including required software, accessories, installation, and on-site operator training, in support of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), Division of Intramural Research. Market research conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10 concluded that the Xact Metal XM200-series LPBF platform is the only commercially available system that simultaneously satisﬁes all of the Government's mandatory salient characteristics — including qualiﬁed processing of titanium alloys, copper, and stainless steel on a single multi-material platform; feature precision of 50 microns or ﬁner; an integrated glovebox for safe handling of reactive metal powders; single-phase 100–240 VAC laboratory power compatibi

monly used engineering metals; • Multi-material capability supporting a range of metal powders without fundamental system modiﬁcation; • Integrated system for safe handling of reactive metal powders, including titanium, through an enclosed or controlled environment (e.g., glovebox or equivalent); • Compact footprint suitable for installation and operation within a biomedical research laboratory; • Compatibility with standard single-phase laboratory electrical infrastructure (100– 240 VAC, 50–60 Hz); • Inclusion of all required software, accessories, and operational components necessary for full system functionality; • Provision of on-site installation and operator training. The system shall be delivered, installed, and made fully operational within sixty (60) days after contract award. Installation and training shall be coordinated with the Government technical point of contact.
